The Tofu-1 speech-to-speech model targets calls from moving cars, hospital rooms and weak-signal lines. It listens while it speaks and reasons while it talks. For phone-agent teams, one model now handles audio in and audio out, with no transcript between. You can check the deployment options and specs here through our GPULeaderboard.com chrome extension . What is Tofu-1? Tofu-1 is a full-duplex speech-to-speech model from Bland that hears, reasons and replies in audio during phone calls. It is the first release in a planned family of Bland speech-to-speech models. How does Tofu-1 differ from a cascade voice agent? Most voice agents are cascades. They turn speech into text, pass it to a language model, then turn the reply back into speech. Tofu-1 listens to the audio directly , so tone, hesitation and background sound stay available to the model. Bland has not published the internal architecture. Audio understanding Bland lists 3 audio skills on its product page: Speaker tracking: tells speakers apart and works out who each one is addressing. Noise separation: separates voices from a crying child, a TV, highway traffic, a hospital intercom or keypad tones. Paralinguistics: hears hesitation, frustration and urgency. Full duplex and thinking while talking Callers can interrupt or correct Tofu-1 mid-sentence. While it works on a request, it keeps the conversation moving. It reports the result only when the work is done. It never claims a task is finished early. Scene generation Because Tofu-1 models the sound of a call, it can also produce one. That includes a second speaker, the room around them and line noise. What is Bland’s ‘TV Test’? The TV Test asks one question: can the model follow the caller while ignoring speech from another scene? TV audio is often louder than the caller. Bland marks its TV Test walkthrough as illustrative, not recorded model output. How does Tofu-1 compare with other full-duplex models? The post Hark Releases Handoff², a 2x Faster Computer-Use Agent for Hark Pro appeared first on MarkTechPost . ]]> Hark has released Handoff² , the second version of the computer-use agent inside its Hark Pro app. The Hark Handoff 2 computer-use agent finishes web tasks about 2x faster than the original, on average. Hark states that the gains come from reinforcement learning (RL) that penalized wasted turns and latency. For teams building browser agents, it is a case study in training for speed, not only accuracy. You can check the deployment options and specs here through our GPULeaderboard.com chrome extension . TL;DR Runs on: Hark’s cloud. Each request gets a dedicated virtual computer. Users reach it from web, iOS and Android. No local or quantized option. Performance: 82% task completion on Hark’s 478-task internal benchmark, about 2x faster end to end than v1. Best: 93.8% on Hark’s internal alignment benchmark (v1: 90.3%). Worst: 82% browsing completion still trails Claude Opus 5.5 (max), by up to 5 points, in the same harness. Bottom line (best): Up to 3.8x faster flight booking and more than 5x faster long research. Bottom line (worst): Every Handoff² number is self-reported. No third-party score exists yet. What is Hark Handoff²? Handoff² is a computer-use agent from Hark that operates websites the way a person does. It clicks, types and scrolls on live pages instead of calling APIs. Hark previewed Handoff in August and shipped it in Hark Pro in October. Since then, Hark says it has logged over 5.6M browsing sessions and handled over $20M in purchases. Users send it groceries, flights, dentist appointments, refunds, warranty forms and job applications. How does Handoff² get 2x faster? Hark co-evolved 2 things: the agent harness and the RL training recipe. The new harness lets the model emit more actions per turn. Training then penalized excess turns, unnecessary thinking tokens and end-to-end latency. The model learned 3 habits: Batch actions, such as filling several form fields in 1 turn. Group repeated action patterns into reusable composite actions. Reuse those composites as the task continues. Each request runs on a dedicated virtual computer with its own browser, file system and terminal. The model outputs cursor and keyboard actions aimed at screen coordinates. Because savings stack per turn, gains grow on longer, browsing-heavy tasks. How fast is Handoff² compared with Handoff? Hark reports these speedups over v1 : Average: about 2x faster end to end.
